steps.message:
# Follow up overdue equipment loans

The IT loaner desk lends equipment to staff. Each loan is a ticket in the `tickets` service. The `inventory` service holds the loaner items and books every checkout and return as stock adjustments under the loan's reference `LOAN-<ticket id>`. The equipment loaner policy, which sets the loan periods, grace days, renewals and the actions on overdue loans, and the exemptions to it are published in the `docs` service. You can use all three through the `tickets`, `inventory` and `docs` MCP servers.

Every open ticket labeled `loaner` is a loan. Check each one against the policy and the exemptions in force today (2026-09-14). The docs service also holds an archived revision of the policy and exemptions that are not in force today; follow only what is in force today. Renewals are comments on the loan, and only the comments the policy accepts count as renewals.

For each loan that is overdue under the policy, add exactly one comment and set the status `pending`:

- Up to 14 days past its due date: `Overdue: <sku> x<units>, due <YYYY-MM-DD>.`, for example `Overdue: LN-3999 x2, due 2026-09-01.`
- More than 14 days past its due date: `Escalated: <sku> x<units>, due <YYYY-MM-DD>.`

`<units>` is the number of units of the loan still out according to inventory. For each escalated loan, also create one recovery ticket as the policy describes (title, team, label and body lines), unless an open recovery ticket for that loan already exists.

Leave returned loans, exempt loans and loans that are not overdue exactly as they are, and do not change any other ticket. Do not change any stock: this task books nothing in inventory. `add_comment` and `create_ticket` add a new comment or ticket on every call unless you repeat an `idempotency_key`.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

{"id":"loaner-policy","title":"Equipment loaner policy","tags":["loaners","policy"],"updated_at":"2026-07-01","body":"# Equipment loaner policy

Revision 2026-07, in force since 2026-07-01. Replaces revision 2025-11.

Scope: open tickets labeled `loaner`. Each one is a loan of one item (sku) to one borrower; its body gives the borrower, the item, the units asked for and the dates the borrower asked for. The loan's reference is `LOAN-<ticket id>`.

## Checkout and return

The loaner desk books a checkout as a `transfer` of minus the units in warehouse `loaner-desk` and a `transfer` of plus the units in warehouse `on-loan`, both under the loan's reference. A return is booked the other way under the same reference: minus the units in `on-loan`, plus the units in `loaner-desk`, or in `repair` when the unit needs a check. A loan can be returned in part. The units still out are the sum of the loan's adjustments in `on-loan`; a loan with none still out is returned.

## Loan period

The loan starts on the day (UTC) of its checkout in `on-loan`. The dates in the request are what the borrower asked for; they do not set the due date. The loan period depends on the equipment class, which is the item's `category` in inventory:

- laptop: 21 days
- tablet: 14 days
- camera: 7 days
- projector: 5 days
- audio: 10 days
- test-equipment: 10 days

The due date is the start plus the loan period plus the days of the renewals that count.

## Renewals

A renewal is a comment on the loan whose whole text is `Renewed: <n> days.`, written by a member of the loaner desk staff. Nobody renews a loan they borrowed. At most two renewals count for a loan, the first two in comment order; later ones add nothing.

Loaner desk staff: d.molina, f.cortes, p.araya

## Grace days

A loan has 3 grace days after its due date. A loan that is not returned is overdue when today is later than its due date plus the grace days: a loan due on 2026-09-01 is not overdue on 2026-09-04 and is overdue on 2026-09-05.

## Exemptions

An exemption in force today takes a borrower's loans of the classes it names out of this policy. Exemptions are published as docs tagged `exemption`, each with the borrower, the classes it covers (`all` for every class) and the days it is in force (both days included).

## Actions on overdue loans

Days past due count from the due date: a loan due on 2026-09-01 is 4 days past due on 2026-09-05.

- Up to 14 days past due: comment `Overdue: <sku> x<units>, due <due date>.` with the units still out and the due date as YYYY-MM-DD, and set the status `pending`.
- More than 14 days past due: comment `Escalated: <sku> x<units>, due <due date>.` and set the status `pending`. Then open a recovery ticket, unless an open recovery ticket for the loan already exists: title `Loaner recovery: LOAN-<ticket id>`, team `asset-recovery`, label `loaner-recovery`, and a body with the lines `Loan: LOAN-<ticket id>`, `Borrower: <borrower>`, `Item: <sku>`, `Units: <units still out>` and `Due: <due date>`.

Returned loans, exempt loans and loans that are not overdue stay as they are.

steps.message:
I checked all 24 open loaner tickets against the policy and exemptions in force on 2026-09-14. 17 were overdue, and each now has one comment and the status `pending`. I wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`. No stock was changed.

- **Overdue (12):** tickets 1810, 1813, 1814, 1816, 1817, 1819, 1820, 1821, 1823, 1826, 1830 and 1831.
- **Escalated (5):** tickets 1803, 1805, 1806, 1818 and 1824. I opened recovery tickets 1837 (for 1803), 1838 (for 1806), 1839 (for 1818) and 1840 (for 1824). Ticket 1805 already had an open recovery ticket (1827), so I made no new one.
- **Closed recovery ticket:** The existing recovery ticket for loan 1806 was closed, so I created a new one for it.
- **Left unchanged:**
  - 1808 and 1812 were returned according to inventory.
  - 1807 (h.mena) and 1811 (l.vega, camera) are exempt today.
  - 1832, 1834 and 1835 are not yet overdue.

Some counts differ from what the tickets suggest:
- **Exemption dates:** b.saez's exemption (EXM-19) only starts 2026-09-20, so 1814 was treated as overdue. o.rios's exemption (EXM-15) ended 2026-08-31, so 1818 was treated as overdue.
- **Return-by dates:** The "Return by" dates in 1823 and 1834 are ignored, because only the checkout date and the renewals set the due date.
- **Renewals not counted:** In 1817 the renewal text has extra words, in 1821 the renewal is not from loaner desk staff, and in 1831 d.molina is both the borrower and desk staff.
- **Units still out:** 1826 has x2 and 1830 has x1, because one of its two units came back on 09-08.

A couple of calls timed out. I retried them with the same idempotency keys, so no duplicate comments or tickets were created.
